analysis.title: What's Trending Across Credit - 1 Nov 2026
key_insights: Credit signals are mixed heading into November: synthetics finished the week tighter while cash spreads widened to multi-month highs, hyperscaler supply tested IG appetite, and HY decompression persisted despite a midweek squeeze. Loans stabilized on CLO demand. The desk describes growing selectivity among investors.

AI financing: Meta's ~$95bn equity financing plan and Oracle's guidance for positive FCF by FY2028 drove a relief rally, which reversed on disappointing tech earnings and $25bn of Microsoft supply. Microsoft is the only major hyperscaler generating positive FCF. The desk sees risk-reward as balanced with a bias to sell rallies, with possible tactical length near YTD wides.

IG issuance reached $60bn across 23 deals this week against $30-35bn expected, led by Microsoft's $25bn deal, its first outright bond deal since 2017. October closed at $132bn. YTD IG issuance is above $2tn, exceeding 2020's full-year record. Global hyperscaler issuance of $254bn is already above GIR's $250bn year-end forecast.

IG OAS widened to 90bps, the widest since late March, while all-in yields fell ~7.5bps to 5.79% on the Treasury rally. CDX IG tightened 1.5bps. The desk reads the cash-synthetic gap as supply indigestion and positioning, not a broad repricing of fundamental credit risk.
EUR IG benefited from beta compression and short covering, but real-money switching skewed toward reducing risk and moving up in quality.

HY OAS tightened from 337bps to 312bps by Wednesday, then reversed to 340bps on Friday, the widest since May 2025, with all-in yield at 8.31%. The early rally came partly from short covering. VRRM bonds fell as much as 9pts on uncertainty around its Avis contract. HY primary issuance was ~$4bn.
The desk sees the relative-value case for owning lower-quality HY beta as challenging, since higher-quality credit offers increasingly attractive all-in yields and decompression continues.

Loans reversed the prior week's weakness: higher-quality paper gained 0.125-0.25pts and higher-beta credits gained 1-2pts. Tuesday's squeeze came from CLO ramp demand, ETF creations and institutional buying in airlines, chemicals and building products. Primary was $2.9bn across six deals. CLO AAAs are ~3-4bps off their tights. Stronger BB structures are better positioned than weaker collateral.

CDX IG tightened 1.5bps to 62bps. HY47 gained 0.29pts to 105.90, about 7bps of spread tightening. Main and Xover tightened 2.5bps and 14.5bps. HY finished nearly 20bps rich to NAV versus ~3bps in IG. Hedge fund short covering drove early compression, and protection buying returned by Friday. Vol, tranche and curve markets did not confirm the spot rally.

The FOMC held at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 decision, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Chair Warsh gave little clarity on December. 2y yields fell ~10bps to 4.58%, 10y yields fell ~6bps to 4.93%, 2s10s steepened ~4bps to 35bps, and MOVE fell toward 100.

Brent reached a six-month high on renewed Middle East tensions, which supports energy credit but complicates the inflation outlook. Brazil's local assets and EM credit came under pressure after Lula's narrow election victory before stabilizing.

Next week's catalysts: US midterms Tuesday, Treasury refunding announcement Wednesday (the franchise recap says Monday), Apple and Palantir earnings, BoE decision Thursday, and October payrolls Friday. The desk frames the question as whether technical demand can keep offsetting a more fragile fundamental backdrop.

Equities: NDX fell ~7% in October, matching its worst month of the AI cycle. Semis fell ~8% on Friday while defensives were bid, with XLV at an all-time high. The S&P broke its medium-term CTA threshold and VVIX rose above 120. The desk pointed to buying protection on hyperscalers into the midterms.

Global Rates Trader: AI-driven risk asset volatility has replaced energy as the main driver of global duration. GIR estimates real money is still underweight duration. The team favors long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly into the refunding and sees 5y outperformance in EUR. It sees a high bar for the BoE to be more hawkish than pricing, gilt 10s skewed to underperform, and JGB long-end outperformance holding during risk-off.

FX: GS FX Research sees the Dollar range-bound with elections driving moves. It sees BRL as Brazil's best-performing asset in coming months and ILS as a hedge for tech-heavy portfolios. A Democratic sweep, the outcome markets price most, would weaken the Dollar with JPY the clearest winner. Republicans keeping Congress would be the biggest surprise and the clearest case for the Dollar to break higher.

Oil: GS raised its Brent forecast to $105 for Dec-26 (from $90) and $88 for the 2027 average (from $80). A risk premium of about $27 explains most of October's rally. The base case includes a 1mb/d supply disruption allowance for 2027, with a $130 upside case and a downside case in the $60s.

GIR Credit Strategy: credit funds have had a tough few months, especially in HY, and large active managers trailed benchmarks in IG and HY. The team suggests less AI-correlated defensives: Utilities, Financials and Healthcare/Pharma in IG, and Energy in HY. It prefers B-rated carry to BBs, stays underweight CCCs, favors BBBs in IG, likes hybrids and US bank sub debt for crossover investors, and prefers USD to EUR credit.

GS MarketStrats (Avishek Biswas): stick with defensive longs (long risk iTraxx Main 5y5y forward at ~155bp, sell Main payer spreads), paired with RV tail hedges: Xover/Main decompression for Middle East risk, and shorts in EUR AT1 and SubFin for France/OAT risk.

IG trading desk (Brad Shelofsky): the 30y hyperscaler basket had its most volatile week of the year, averaging 6.3bp a day. It rallied 17bp on Meta's equity financing plan and Oracle's investor day, then reversed on weak core-business earnings, Meta turning FCF-negative and the $25bn Microsoft supply. Desk bias is to sell rallies but look for tactical length at the wides.

GS Securitized Research: stay modestly overweight agency MBS, with ABS as refuge from heavy IG supply. The team sees corporate spreads as more stretched than ABS and expects AI-related issuance to widen corporates. Datacenter ABS has widened to attractive levels on the broader AI-debt repricing, and the team recommends staying up in quality and avoiding leverage. Home improvement ABS was downgraded to neutral.

GS CLO Secondary: loans and CLOs share a technical floor, with accounts sitting on cash and AAAs barely moving through macro vol. The look-through is a steeper credit curve and wider quality dispersion, with BB MVOCs widely spread across deals.

Rates note: the Fed held 10-2, and Warsh said there will be fewer meetings with a rate vote from next fall. The AI-earnings selloff (Alphabet, ServiceNow, Amazon, Intel) pushed investors into Treasuries, and the S&P fell 2.24% on Friday. Microsoft's $25bn ten-part deal drew $115bn of orders.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for high-quality paper remains intact. Microsoft's $25bn deal drew $115bn of orders, and spreads near YTD wides may offer tactical opportunities for selective length.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler issuance of $254bn is above GIR's $250bn year-end forecast, and investors are being tested on how much incremental supply they will warehouse without greater spread concessions. Meta turned FCF-negative and the desk's bias is to sell rallies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler issuance absorbed without spread concessions, or a path to self-funding such as Oracle's positive FCF guidance for FY2028 gaining credibility.

tension_points.bear_case: Quality dispersion is building, and liquidity for weaker collateral remains challenged.
